blocks.title: Use modern constructs to express a clear model
paragraphs: Modern Java can remove boilerplate without removing type rules. Choose var, enum, records or sealed types for what they communicate, and keep the underlying contracts visible.

blocks.title: Choose a closed value set or a data carrier deliberately
paragraphs: An enum models a named finite set such as PENDING, ACTIVE and CLOSED; it can have fields and methods. A record declares a data carrier whose component fields are final and whose accessors, equals, hashCode and toString are generated. A record is final and cannot extend an arbitrary class.

Records are shallowly immutable: a final List component can still refer to a mutable list unless you copy or restrict it. Generated equality follows component equality; it does not invent the domain identity you wanted. Choose a normal class when controlled state changes or a different identity policy are central.

A final class cannot be subclassed. A sealed class/interface restricts its permitted direct subtypes. Keep the choice tied to a real model; a closed set of variants can make exhaustive handling easier.

blocks.title: var infers once; switch expressions produce values
paragraphs: var is local type inference from an initializer, not a dynamically changing type. var count = 4 still means an int variable; assigning a String later fails. An uninitialized var declaration and an untyped lambda assigned directly to var do not supply enough type information.

The enum switch below is exhaustive and each arrow branch supplies one result without fall-through. A switch expression is a value and can initialize a variable. Make the covered cases clear; do not confuse it with an older statement switch that may fall through.

blocks.title: Comparable defines an ordering
paragraphs: compareTo returns a negative value, zero or a positive value, not necessarily exactly −1 or 1. Zero means equivalent under this ordering, which is not automatically the same as equals. Choose and document tie-breaking so clients understand the order.

This original Slot compares aisle text first and then its integer position. Integer.compare avoids the overflow risk of subtracting arbitrary integers as a comparator. The ordering here includes all record components.

blocks.title: Less boilerplate still requires a contract
paragraphs: Use local inference without losing static types, record components without claiming deep immutability, exhaustive switch expressions without fall-through, and comparison results by their sign.

cards.prompt: Does a record containing a mutable ArrayList freeze that list?
cards.answer: No. Its component reference is final, but the referenced list can still change. Use an appropriate defensive copy or immutable collection when the contract requires stable contents.

cards.prompt: How do final and sealed differ for a class?
cards.answer: final prevents subclasses. sealed restricts which direct subtypes are permitted; those subtypes must satisfy the language’s continuation rules. Use the distinction to express the intended model.

cards.prompt: Does var let a local variable change from int to String?
cards.answer: No. Its static type is inferred from its initializer and remains that type. var changes how you write the declaration, not the type system.
No. Only the sign and zero matter. Zero means tied under the ordering; make its relationship to equals and any tie-breaking deliberate.

guided.title: Choose constructs for a booking label
guided.prompt: A label has immutable text and an integer priority. A booking has a status from a small known set and changes status over time. Explain where a record, enum, normal class and Comparable could fit; define the ordering and null policy.
rubric: The mutable booking is not assumed immutable merely because modern syntax is available.
The label’s identity and ordering are stated, with a tie-break if needed.
Null and any mutable referenced contents have an explicit policy.
reference: A Label record can hold validated non-null text and priority; a Status enum expresses the allowed status names; a Booking class controls valid state transitions.

An ordering can compare priority then text. If the record had a list component, final references would not by themselves freeze it. Multiple designs are acceptable when the same contracts are satisfied.
